content: # ============================================================================= # Policy Priorities — a multivariate benefit-cost ranking of 60 policies # Tyler Young · Lighthearted Humans thesis project # # Runs as a normal Shiny app in RStudio (Run App) and is exported to the # website with shinylive (see R/03_export_dashboard.R), where it runs entirely # in the visitor's browser. # ============================================================================= suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(shiny) library(bslib) library(ggplot2) library(DT) }) source("bca_engine.R") pol <- read.csv("policies.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) src <- read.csv("sources.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) GRADE_COLS <- c(A = "#1b7837", B = "#7fbc41", C = "#e08214", D = "#b2182b") cats <- sort(unique(pol$category)) short <- function(x, n = 70) ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n - 1), "…"), x) fmt_bcr <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", ifelse(abs(x) >= 100, formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1))) link_src <- function(url, doi) { u <- ifelse(!is.na(doi) & nzchar(doi), paste0("https://doi.org/", doi), url) ifelse(is.na(u) | !nzchar(u), "", sprintf('link', u)) } theme_lh <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13, base_family = "sans") + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", plot.title.position = "plot", axis.title = element_text(size = 11)) slog_breaks <- c(-100, -10, -1, 0, 1, 10, 100, 1000) # ---- UI ------------------------------------------------------------------------ controls <- sidebar( width = 320, accordion( open = c("Evidence & uncertainty", "Criteria weights"), accordion_panel( "Evidence & uncertainty", radioButtons("basis", "Which numbers?", c("Literature where available, author otherwise" = "blend", "Literature only" = "evidence", "Author's original estimates" = "author"), "blend"), sliderInput("skep", "Evidence skepticism", 0, 1, 0.5, 0.05), helpText("Pulls weakly-sourced BCRs toward 1:1. 0 = take every number at face value."), selectInput("nsim", "Monte Carlo draws", c(500, 1000, 2000), 1000) ), accordion_panel( "Time & fairness", sliderInput("rate", "Discount rate (%)", 0, 10, 5, 0.5), sliderInput("lag", "Years until benefits arrive", 0, 30, 10, 1), sliderInput("eta", "Equity weight (η)", 0, 2, 0, 0.1), helpText("η = 0: a dollar is a dollar. UK Treasury Green Book uses η ≈ 1.3.") ), accordion_panel( "Criteria weights", radioButtons("method", "Scoring method", c("Weighted sum" = "weighted_sum", "TOPSIS" = "topsis"), inline = TRUE), sliderInput("w_value", "Benefit-cost value", 0, 1, 0.60, 0.05), sliderInput("w_equity", "Helps the poor", 0, 1, 0.15, 0.05), sliderInput("w_feas", "Feasibility", 0, 1, 0.10, 0.05), sliderInput("w_evid", "Strength of evidence", 0, 1, 0.15, 0.05), sliderInput("w_cost", "Low cost", 0, 1, 0, 0.05) ), accordion_panel( "Filters", selectizeInput("cats", "Policy areas", cats, cats, multiple = TRUE), checkboxGroupInput("grades", "Evidence grade", c("A", "B", "C", "D"), c("A", "B", "C", "D"), inline = TRUE), sliderInput("topn", "Show top", 5, 60, 25, 1) ) ) ) ui <- page_navbar( title = "Policy Priorities", theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "yeti", base_font = "Georgia, serif", heading_font = "Georgia, serif", primary = "#2c5f7c"), sidebar = controls, fillable = FALSE, nav_panel( "Ranking", layout_columns( value_box("Top-ranked policy", textOutput("vb_top"), theme = "primary"), value_box("Policies ranked", textOutput("vb_n"), theme = "secondary"), value_box("Backed by published BCRs", textOutput("vb_ev"), theme = "success"), col_widths = c(6, 3, 3) ), card(card_header("Adjusted benefit-cost ratio (median and 90% interval), ordered by overall score"), plotOutput("rank_plot", height = "760px")), card(card_header("Ranking table"), DTOutput("rank_table")) ), nav_panel( "Uncertainty", card(card_header("How stable is each rank? (90% range across Monte Carlo draws)"), plotOutput("unc_plot", height = "760px")), card(card_header("Probability of landing in the top N"), plotOutput("ptop_plot", height = "520px")) ), nav_panel( "Author vs. literature", card(card_header("Author's original midpoint vs. the literature's midpoint (policies with positive BCRs in both)"), plotOutput("avl_plot", height = "560px")), card(card_header("Where the sources disagree with the spreadsheet"), DTOutput("flag_table")) ), nav_panel( "Budget", layout_columns( card(sliderInput("budget", "Budget ($ billions per year)", 1, 150, 50, 1), sliderInput("minbcr", "Fund only if adjusted BCR is above", 1, 20, 1, 0.5)), value_box("Spent", textOutput("vb_spent"), theme = "secondary"), value_box("Estimated benefits", textOutput("vb_benefit"), theme = "success"), col_widths = c(6, 3, 3) ), card(card_header("Funded, in order of adjusted benefit-cost ratio"), DTOutput("funded_table")), card(card_header("Reforms with no estimated fiscal cost (rank by BCR; these don't use the budget)"), DTOutput("free_table")) ), nav_panel( "Policy explorer", selectInput("pick", NULL, setNames(pol$id, paste0("#", pol$id, " ", pol$title)), width = "100%"), uiOutput("policy_card"), card(card_header("Sources"), DTOutput("policy_sources")) ), nav_panel( "All sources", card(card_header(textOutput("src_count")), DTOutput("all_sources")) ), nav_panel( "Method", card(card_body( h4("What this is"), p("A comparative benefit-cost analysis built on published estimates: the benefit-cost ratios (BCRs) come from other researchers' studies, put on one scale and ranked. Adding income, feasibility, evidence and cost criteria makes it a light multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA)."), h4("Steps"), tags$ol( tags$li(strong("Numbers. "), "Each policy has the author's original BCR range and, where the literature supports one, an evidence range from the cited sources (468 citations across 60 policies). 'Blend' uses the literature where it exists."), tags$li(strong("Evidence quality. "), "Each policy is graded A (several peer-reviewed BCRs) to D (qualitative only). The author's own unsourced ranges are treated as grade C at best, and D where the literature contradicts them. The skepticism dial pulls weaker numbers toward break-even (1:1) in log space."), tags$li(strong("Time. "), "Published BCRs are already discounted. To test other discount rates, benefits are assumed to arrive on average 'lag' years after costs: factor = ((1 + 5%) / (1 + r))^lag. This is an approximation, not a re-estimation."), tags$li(strong("Fairness. "), "Standard welfare weights (1/relative income)^η, with low / middle / upper incomes at 0.3 / 1 / 3 times the mean and population shares 40/40/20. Benefit shares come from the author's income-group scores."), tags$li(strong("Uncertainty. "), "Each range is treated as a 90% interval of a lognormal distribution and sampled (Monte Carlo). Every draw is re-ranked, giving each policy a probability of being in the top N and a rank interval."), tags$li(strong("Scoring. "), "Five criteria rescaled 0–1 (value, pro-poor benefit, feasibility, evidence strength, low cost), combined by weighted sum or TOPSIS (closeness to an ideal policy)."), tags$li(strong("Budget. "), "With a fixed budget, fund policies in order of adjusted BCR until the money runs out.") ), h4("Caveats"), p("Many policies here have never been tried at full scale, so no study measures them directly; those rely on the author's estimates and carry low evidence grades. Ranges from different studies use different assumptions. Zero-cost entries are regulatory reforms whose transition costs have not been estimated. Treat the ranking as a transparent, adjustable argument about priorities, not a forecast."), p(em("Source code, data and every citation: the LH_CBA R project.")) )) ) ) # ---- Server -------------------------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output, session) { res <- reactive({ w <- c(value = input$w_value, equity = input$w_equity, feasibility = input$w_feas, evidence = input$w_evid, cost = input$w_cost) run_bca(pol, basis = input$basis, skepticism = input$skep, rate = input$rate / 100, lag = input$lag, eta = input$eta, n_sims = as.integer(input$nsim), weights = w, method = input$method, top_n = input$topn) }) shown <- reactive({ r <- res() r <- r[!is.na(r$rank) & r$category %in% input$cats & r$grade_used %in% input$grades, ] r$shown_rank <- seq_len(nrow(r)) r }) output$vb_top <- renderText({ r <- shown(); if (nrow(r)) short(r$title[1], 60) else "—" }) output$vb_n <- renderText(nrow(shown())) output$vb_ev <- renderText({ r <- shown(); sprintf("%d of %d", sum(r$range_source == "evidence"), nrow(r)) }) output$rank_plot <- renderPlot({ r <- head(shown(), input$topn) validate(need(nrow(r) > 0, "No policies match these filters.")) r$lab <- factor(paste0(r$shown_rank, ". ", short(r$title, 60)), levels = rev(paste0(r$shown_rank, ". ", short(r$title, 60)))) ggplot(r, aes(y = lab, x = slog(bcr_median), colour = grade_used)) + geom_vline(xintercept = slog(1), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_segment(aes(x = slog(bcr_q05), xend = slog(bcr_q95), yend = lab), linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.6) + geom_point(aes(shape = range_source), size = 3) + scale_x_continuous("Adjusted benefit-cost ratio (log scale; dashed line = break-even)", breaks = slog(slog_breaks), labels = slog_breaks) + scale_colour_manual("Evidence grade", values = GRADE_COLS, drop = FALSE) + scale_shape_manual("Numbers from", values = c(evidence = 16, author = 1, none = 4)) + labs(y = NULL) + theme_lh }) output$rank_table <- renderDT({ r <- shown() d <- data.frame(Rank = r$shown_rank, `#` = r$id, Policy = r$title, Area = r$category, Grade = r$grade_used, `Numbers from` = r$range_source, `BCR median` = fmt_bcr(r$bcr_median), `90% range` = paste(fmt_bcr(r$bcr_q05), "to", fmt_bcr(r$bcr_q95)), `P(top N)` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * r$p_top), Score = round(r$score, 3), `Original rank` = r$author_rank, check.names = FALSE) datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE)) }) output$unc_plot <- renderPlot({ r <- head(shown(), input$topn) validate(need(nrow(r) > 0, "No policies match these filters.")) r$lab <- factor(short(r$title, 60), levels = rev(short(r$title, 60))) ggplot(r, aes(y = lab)) + geom_segment(aes(x = rank_lo, xend = rank_hi, yend = lab, colour = grade_used), linewidth = 3, alpha = 0.5) + geom_point(aes(x = rank_median), size = 2.5) + scale_colour_manual("Evidence grade", values = GRADE_COLS) + labs(x = "Rank across simulations (median and 90% range; all 60 policies)", y = NULL) + theme_lh }) output$ptop_plot <- renderPlot({ r <- shown(); r <- head(r[order(-r$p_top), ], 25) r$lab <- factor(short(r$title, 60), levels = rev(short(r$title, 60))) ggplot(r, aes(x = p_top, y = lab, fill = grade_used)) + geom_col() + scale_x_continuous(paste0("Probability of ranking in the top ", input$topn), labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%"), limits = c(0, 1)) + scale_fill_manual("Evidence grade", values = GRADE_COLS) + labs(y = NULL) + theme_lh }) output$avl_plot <- renderPlot({ d <- pol[!is.na(pol$evidence_bcr_low) & pol$author_bcr_low > 0 & pol$evidence_bcr_low > 0, ] d$a <- sqrt(d$author_bcr_low * d$author_bcr_high) d$e <- sqrt(d$evidence_bcr_low * d$evidence_bcr_high) ggplot(d, aes(a, e, colour = evidence_grade)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_point(size = 3) + geom_text(aes(label = id), vjust = -0.9, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_log10("Author's estimate (geometric midpoint)") + scale_y_log10("Literature estimate (geometric midpoint)") + scale_colour_manual("Evidence grade", values = GRADE_COLS) + theme_lh + labs(caption = "Above the dashed line: the literature is more optimistic than the spreadsheet. Below: less.") }) output$flag_table <- renderDT({ d <- pol[pol$match != "supports", c("id", "title", "match", "evidence_grade", "flag_note")] names(d) <- c("#", "Policy", "Match", "Grade", "What the sources say") datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) }) pf <- reactive(portfolio(res(), input$budget, input$minbcr)) output$vb_spent <- renderText(sprintf("$%.1f bn", pf()$spent)) output$vb_benefit <- renderText(sprintf("$%s bn", formatC(pf()$benefit, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","))) output$funded_table <- renderDT({ f <- pf()$funded datatable(data.frame(`#` = f$id, Policy = f$title, `Cost ($bn)` = f$cost, `Adjusted BCR` = fmt_bcr(f$bcr), `Benefit ($bn)` = round(f$benefit), check.names = FALSE), rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, dom = "tp")) }) output$free_table <- renderDT({ f <- pf()$free datatable(data.frame(`#` = f$id, Policy = f$title, `Adjusted BCR` = fmt_bcr(f$bcr), check.names = FALSE), rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tp")) }) output$policy_card <- renderUI({ p <- pol[pol$id == as.integer(input$pick), ] r <- res(); rr <- r[r$id == p$id, ] card( card_header(paste0("#", p$id, " · ", p$title)), layout_columns( value_box("Current rank", if (is.na(rr$rank)) "—" else rr$rank), value_box("Author's range", paste(fmt_bcr(p$author_bcr_low), "to", fmt_bcr(p$author_bcr_high))), value_box("Literature range", if (is.na(p$evidence_bcr_low)) "none published" else paste(fmt_bcr(p$evidence_bcr_low), "to", fmt_bcr(p$evidence_bcr_high))), value_box("Evidence grade", paste0(p$evidence_grade, " (", gsub("_", " ", p$match), ")")), col_widths = c(3, 3, 3, 3) ), p(strong("What it does: "), p$explanation), p(strong("What the sources say: "), p$flag_note), if (nzchar(p$cost_note)) p(strong("Cost: "), p$cost_note), if (nzchar(p$income_note)) p(strong("Who benefits: "), p$income_note), tags$details(tags$summary("Author's original notes (unverified)"), p(p$author_source_notes)) ) }) output$policy_sources <- renderDT({ s <- src[src$policy_id == as.integer(input$pick), ] datatable(data.frame(Authors = s$authors, Year = s$year, Title = s$title, Venue = s$venue, Type = gsub("_", " ", s$type), `Reports` = s$reported_estimate, Link = link_src(s$url, s$doi), check.names = FALSE), rownames = FALSE, escape = -7, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) }) output$src_count <- renderText(sprintf("%d citations across %d policies", nrow(src), length(unique(src$policy_id)))) output$all_sources <- renderDT({ datatable(data.frame(`#` = src$policy_id, Policy = short(pol$title[match(src$policy_id, pol$id)], 45), Authors = src$authors, Year = src$year, Title = src$title, Venue = src$venue, Type = gsub("_", " ", src$type), Link = link_src(src$url, src$doi), check.names = FALSE), rownames = FALSE, escape = -8, filter = "top", options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE)) }) } shinyApp(ui, server)

name: bca_engine.R
content:
# =============================================================================
# bca_engine.R — the analysis engine for the Lighthearted Humans policy ranking
#
# A comparative benefit-cost analysis built on published estimates, extended
# into a light multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA).  Every step is a plain
# function so the same code drives the paper (02_run_analysis.R) and the
# dashboard (app/app.R).
#
# Pipeline for one set of user settings:
#   1. choose_range()      which BCR range to use (author / evidence / blend)
#   2. shrink_by_grade()   evidence-quality adjustment (skepticism dial)
#   3. time_adjust()       re-express at a different discount rate
#   4. equity_multiplier() distributional weights (elasticity of marginal utility)
#   5. simulate()          Monte Carlo over each policy's range
#   6. mcda_score()        combine value, equity, feasibility, evidence, cost
#   7. rank_stats()        rank probabilities across simulations
#   8. portfolio()         what a fixed budget buys
# =============================================================================

GRADE_WEIGHT <- c(A = 1.00, B = 0.85, C = 0.60, D = 0.40)

# --- 1. Which range ----------------------------------------------------------
# basis = "author"   : Tyler's original spreadsheet range
#         "evidence" : range supported by the cited literature (NA if none)
#         "blend"    : evidence where it exists, author's range otherwise
choose_range <- function(p, basis = c("blend", "author", "evidence")) {
  basis <- match.arg(basis)
  ev_ok <- !is.na(p$evidence_bcr_low) & !is.na(p$evidence_bcr_high)
  lo <- switch(basis,
               author   = p$author_bcr_low,
               evidence = ifelse(ev_ok, p$evidence_bcr_low, NA),
               blend    = ifelse(ev_ok, p$evidence_bcr_low, p$author_bcr_low))
  hi <- switch(basis,
               author   = p$author_bcr_high,
               evidence = ifelse(ev_ok, p$evidence_bcr_high, NA),
               blend    = ifelse(ev_ok, p$evidence_bcr_high, p$author_bcr_high))
  src <- switch(basis,
                author   = rep("author", nrow(p)),
                evidence = ifelse(ev_ok, "evidence", "none"),
                blend    = ifelse(ev_ok, "evidence", "author"))
  data.frame(lo = pmin(lo, hi), hi = pmax(lo, hi), range_source = src)
}

# --- 2. Evidence-quality shrinkage -------------------------------------------
# Weaker evidence pulls a BCR toward break-even (1:1) in log space.
# skepticism = 0 ignores evidence quality; 1 applies full grade weights.
# Negative BCRs (net harms) shrink their magnitude the same way.
shrink_by_grade <- function(bcr, grade, skepticism = 0.5) {
  w <- GRADE_WEIGHT[grade]; w[is.na(w)] <- 0.40
  weff <- 1 - skepticism * (1 - w)
  mag <- exp(weff * log(pmax(abs(bcr), 1e-9)))
  ifelse(is.na(bcr), NA, ifelse(bcr > 0, mag, -mag))
}

# Effective grade for the numbers actually used: the author's own (unsourced)
# range never earns better than C, and a range the literature contradicts is D.
effective_grade <- function(p, range_source) {
  g <- p$evidence_grade
  g[is.na(g)] <- "D"
  ord <- c(A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, D = 4)
  own <- range_source == "author"
  g[own] <- names(ord)[pmax(ord[g[own]], 3)]
  g[own & !is.na(p$match) & p$match == "no"] <- "D"
  g
}

# --- 3. Discount-rate re-expression -------------------------------------------
# Published BCRs are already discounted (mostly 3-8%).  Without each study's
# cash-flow timing we approximate: benefits arrive on average `lag` years after
# costs, originally discounted at `base_rate`.  Re-expressing at `rate`:
#   factor = ((1 + base_rate) / (1 + rate))^lag
time_adjust <- function(bcr, rate = 0.05, base_rate = 0.05, lag = 10) {
  bcr * ((1 + base_rate) / (1 + rate))^lag
}

# --- 4. Distributional (equity) weights ---------------------------------------
# Standard welfare weights: w_g = (ybar / y_g)^eta  (HM Treasury Green Book,
# eta ~ 1.3).  Group incomes relative to the mean: low 0.3, middle 1, upper 3;
# population shares 40/40/20.  Each policy's benefit shares come from the
# author's income-group scores; the multiplier is 1 when eta = 0.
equity_multiplier <- function(p, eta = 0,
                              rel_income = c(0.3, 1, 3), pop = c(0.4, 0.4, 0.2)) {
  if (eta == 0) return(rep(1, nrow(p)))
  w <- (1 / rel_income)^eta
  w <- w / sum(pop * w)
  sc <- abs(cbind(p$inc_low, p$inc_mid, p$inc_upper))
  sc[is.na(sc)] <- 0
  tot <- rowSums(sc)
  sh <- sc / ifelse(tot == 0, 1, tot)
  if (any(tot == 0)) sh[tot == 0, ] <- matrix(pop, nrow = sum(tot == 0), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  as.vector(sh %*% w)
}

# --- 5. Monte Carlo ------------------------------------------------------------
# Each range is treated as a 90% interval of a lognormal (positive ranges) or a
# negated lognormal (harm ranges).  Point estimates get a small spread.
simulate <- function(lo, hi, n = 2000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  k <- length(lo)
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, n, k)
  for (j in seq_len(k)) {
    a <- lo[j]; b <- hi[j]
    if (is.na(a) || is.na(b)) next
    if (a > 0 || b < 0) {
      s  <- sign(ifelse(a > 0, 1, -1))
      la <- log(abs(a)); lb <- log(abs(b))
      mu <- (la + lb) / 2
      sd <- max(abs(lb - la) / (2 * 1.645), 0.10)
      out[, j] <- s * exp(rnorm(n, mu, sd))
    } else {                                  # range straddles zero
      out[, j] <- rnorm(n, (a + b) / 2, max((b - a) / (2 * 1.645), 0.1))
    }
  }
  out
}

# Signed log so harms and benefits sit on one comparable scale
slog <- function(x) sign(x) * log10(1 + abs(x))

# --- 6. Multi-criteria score -----------------------------------------------------
# Criteria (all rescaled 0-1):
#   value       signed log of adjusted BCR
#   equity      share of benefits to low-income households (from author scores)
#   feasibility author's -1/0/+1 score
#   evidence    grade A=1 ... D=0.4
#   cost        lower implementation cost scores higher (0 cost = 1)
rescale01 <- function(x) {
  r <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (diff(r) == 0) return(rep(0.5, length(x)))
  (x - r[1]) / diff(r)
}

criteria_matrix <- function(p, bcr_point) {
  sc <- cbind(p$inc_low, p$inc_mid, p$inc_upper); sc[is.na(sc)] <- 0
  eq <- (sc[, 1] - sc[, 3]) + rowSums(sc) / 3          # pro-poor tilt + overall benefit
  data.frame(
    value       = rescale01(slog(bcr_point)),
    equity      = rescale01(eq),
    feasibility = rescale01(ifelse(is.na(p$feasibility), 0, p$feasibility)),
    evidence    = unname(ifelse(is.na(GRADE_WEIGHT[p$evidence_grade]), 0.4, GRADE_WEIGHT[p$evidence_grade])),
    cost        = 1 - rescale01(log10(1 + pmax(ifelse(is.na(p$author_cost_bn), 0, p$author_cost_bn), 0)))
  )
}

# method = "weighted_sum" | "topsis"
mcda_score <- function(C, weights, method = c("weighted_sum", "topsis")) {
  method <- match.arg(method)
  w <- weights[names(C)]; w[is.na(w)] <- 0
  if (sum(w) == 0) w[] <- 1
  w <- w / sum(w)
  ok <- stats::complete.cases(C)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(C))
  M <- as.matrix(C[ok, , drop = FALSE])
  if (!any(ok)) return(out)
  if (method == "weighted_sum") { out[ok] <- as.vector(M %*% w); return(out) }
  # TOPSIS: closeness to the ideal policy and distance from the anti-ideal
  V <- sweep(M, 2, w, `*`)
  ideal <- apply(V, 2, max); anti <- apply(V, 2, min)
  d_pos <- sqrt(rowSums(sweep(V, 2, ideal)^2))
  d_neg <- sqrt(rowSums(sweep(V, 2, anti)^2))
  out[ok] <- d_neg / (d_pos + d_neg + 1e-12)
  out
}

# --- 7. Rank statistics across simulations -------------------------------------
rank_stats <- function(draws, top_n = 10) {
  ok <- colSums(!is.na(draws)) > 0
  R <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(draws), ncol(draws))
  R[, ok] <- t(apply(draws[, ok, drop = FALSE], 1, function(r) rank(-r, ties.method = "average")))
  data.frame(
    p_top       = colMeans(R <= top_n),
    rank_median = apply(R, 2, median),
    rank_lo     = apply(R, 2, quantile, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    rank_hi     = apply(R, 2, quantile, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# --- 8. Budget portfolio -----------------------------------------------------------
# Fund policies in order of adjusted BCR (only those above `min_bcr`) until the
# budget is spent.  Zero-cost (regulatory) reforms are listed separately.
portfolio <- function(res, budget_bn = 50, min_bcr = 1) {
  d <- data.frame(id = res$id, title = res$title, cost = res$author_cost_bn, bcr = res$bcr_median)
  d <- d[!is.na(d$bcr) & d$bcr > min_bcr, ]
  d <- d[order(-d$bcr), ]
  paid <- d[!is.na(d$cost) & d$cost > 0, ]
  paid$cum_cost <- cumsum(paid$cost)
  paid$funded <- paid$cum_cost <= budget_bn
  paid$benefit <- paid$cost * paid$bcr
  list(funded = paid[paid$funded, ],
       unfunded = paid[!paid$funded, ],
       free = d[is.na(d$cost) | d$cost <= 0, ],
       spent = sum(paid$cost[paid$funded]),
       benefit = sum(paid$benefit[paid$funded]))
}

# --- The author's original spreadsheet method (for comparison) -------------------
# BCR midpoint x (100, 80, 60) for 3/5/7%, times (1 + 0.15*income score +
# 0.10*feasibility).  Kept so readers can see how the original ranking arose.
original_method <- function(p, rate = c("3%", "5%", "7%")) {
  rate <- match.arg(rate)
  mid <- (p$author_bcr_low + p$author_bcr_high) / 2
  f <- c(`3%` = 100, `5%` = 80, `7%` = 60)[rate]
  inc <- rowSums(cbind(p$inc_low, p$inc_mid, p$inc_upper), na.rm = TRUE)
  mid * f * (1 + 0.15 * inc + 0.10 * ifelse(is.na(p$feasibility), 0, p$feasibility))
}

# --- One call that runs the whole pipeline ---------------------------------------
run_bca <- function(p, basis = "blend", skepticism = 0.5, rate = 0.05, base_rate = 0.05,
                    lag = 10, eta = 0, n_sims = 2000, seed = 42,
                    weights = c(value = 0.60, equity = 0.15, feasibility = 0.10, evidence = 0.15, cost = 0),
                    method = "weighted_sum", top_n = 10) {
  r  <- choose_range(p, basis)
  eq <- equity_multiplier(p, eta)
  g_eff <- effective_grade(p, r$range_source)
  adj <- function(x) time_adjust(shrink_by_grade(x, g_eff, skepticism), rate, base_rate, lag) * eq
  lo <- adj(r$lo); hi <- adj(r$hi)
  draws <- simulate(lo, hi, n_sims, seed)
  med  <- apply(draws, 2, median)
  q05  <- apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  q95  <- apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
  pg <- p; pg$evidence_grade <- g_eff
  C    <- criteria_matrix(pg, med)
  score <- mcda_score(C, weights, method)
  # rank uncertainty: re-score every simulation draw with the other criteria fixed
  sim_scores <- t(apply(draws, 1, function(d) {
    Cd <- C; Cd$value <- rescale01(slog(d)); mcda_score(Cd, weights, method)
  }))
  rs <- rank_stats(sim_scores, top_n)
  out <- cbind(p[, c("id", "title", "category", "evidence_grade", "match", "author_cost_bn", "author_rank")],
               range_source = r$range_source, grade_used = g_eff, bcr_lo_input = r$lo, bcr_hi_input = r$hi,
               equity_mult = eq, bcr_median = med, bcr_q05 = q05, bcr_q95 = q95,
               C, score = score, rs)
  out$rank <- rank(-out$score, ties.method = "min", na.last = "keep")
  out[is.na(out$bcr_median), c("score", "rank")] <- NA
  out[order(out$rank), ]
}

Cato (Miron & Soares 2021) notes crediting net emissions adds compliance and monitoring costs. Mandating offsets for ALL emissions has not been modelled.","Mandated offset purchases act as a cost pass-through to consumers (regressive like other carbon costs) while payments flow to project developers and verifiers; REDD+ and cookstove credits (the categories with lowest real-reduction shares per Probst et al.) are concentrated in low-income countries, where investigative reporting has linked some projects to land-rights disputes. IETA (2023) argues trading can channel >$100bn/yr to developing countries if integrity holds.",7,4,"Climate & Mandates",FALSE,TRUE
58,"Mandatory ESG reporting for all firms","Forces environmental/social governance disclosure",-10,-1,2000,"Without, avoid $2T/yr compliance; expected global GDP loss $5T","Cato 2025 BCR -1 to -10; Heritage 2024 $5T loss; IMF 2025 multiplier -2.5×; regression on EU CSDDD BCR; SEC rule 2024 $2T cost verified; Deloitte 2025 $5T global loss; (-1–-10).",-3,-2,-1,-1,54,,,"partial","B","No BCR exists: the SEC's own 2024 economic analysis states it is 'unable to quantify' the benefits, so no official BCR can be computed, and the author's 'Cato 2025 BCR -1 to -10', 'Heritage 2024 $5T loss', 'Deloitte 2025 $5T' and 'SEC rule 2024 $2T cost' could not be located — the SEC's figures are ~$197k-$739k per registrant per year (proposal: +$6.4bn/yr aggregate), orders of magnitude below $2T. Direction is supported by evidence that ESG metrics are noisy (ratings correlate only 0.38-0.71; Berg et al.) and weakly linked to real outcomes (Raghunandan & Rajgopal), and by the EU cutting ~80% of firms from CSRD in 2025 and the SEC moving to rescind its rule; counterpoint: Downar et al. (2021) find the UK carbon-disclosure mandate cut emissions ~8% with no hit to margins.","SEC final rule (2024): governance/strategy/risk disclosures ~$327,000 first year and ~$183,000/yr thereafter; average annual cost over 10 years from <$197,000 to >$739,000 per registrant ($872,000 first year at the upper end). SEC 2022 proposal (incl. Scope 3): total disclosure compliance costs rising from ~$3.8bn to ~$10.2bn/yr (+$6.4bn). Winden (2022 comment) estimates ~$25bn/yr forgone US GDP by late 2020s. SMEs and private firms) would multiply costs; no estimate exists, and no source supports $2T/yr.","Compliance costs are largely fixed, so they fall hardest on small and mid-sized firms (the reason the EU exempted ~80% of companies and the SEC phased in smaller filers); Scope 3 requirements push data-collection costs onto unlisted small suppliers (CEI). 59,"Limit domestic/international flights (aviation tax/cap)","Caps/reduces air travel for climate",-30,-3,1000,"Without, avoid $1T/yr loss + mobility drop; expected global GDP loss $5T","IEA 2025 BCR -3 to -30; Cato 2024 $5T loss; IMF 2025 multiplier -5×; regression on EU flight caps BCR; EU ETS aviation 2024 $1T/yr cost verified; Oxford trial 2023 CGE models; (-3–-30).",-3,-2,-1,-1,52,,,"partial","B","No published BCR was found for flight caps or aviation taxes, and the author's 'IEA 2025 BCR -3 to -30', 'Cato 2024 $5T loss' and 'EU ETS aviation $1T/yr cost' could not be located (EU-level modelling puts GDP effects at -0.04% to -0.06%, not trillions). Framing issue: standard economics (Keen, Parry & Strand 2013, IMF economists) holds that a moderate carbon charge on jet fuel (~$25/tCO2) is welfare-IMPROVING given aviation's current tax exemptions, so a Pigouvian aviation tax likely has BCR > 1, whereas quantity caps and high ticket taxes are blunt (ticket taxes cut ~6% of sector CO2 in EC modelling while shedding 1-2% of aviation jobs) and support the author only for the 'cap/limit' version; ACI/InterVISTAS (industry) finds foregone economic impact ~2x the tax revenue collected, and Sweden (2025) and the Netherlands reversed or stalled such measures.","EC/Ricardo (2021) for 2030: stepped ticket tax cuts intra-EEA passengers 8.3% and total aviation CO2 6.2%, GDP -0.06%, air-transport employment -1.8%; €0.33/l fuel tax cuts CO2 3.7% total, GDP -0.04%. ACI/InterVISTAS: ~$90bn/yr global passenger taxes suppress ~760m passengers and ~$183bn economic impact. Bernardo et al. (2024): ticket taxes reduce flights per airline-route 12% and CO2 14%. Hard caps (e.g., Schiphol 500k to 440k movements) forgo consumer surplus with no revenue offset; no study monetises this, and nothing supports $1T/yr.","Per-ticket taxes are regressive within aviation: Bernardo et al. (2024) find the burden is higher for passengers paying low fares (low-cost carrier users), while premium travelers are barely affected; caps ration flights toward higher-willingness-to-pay travelers. Regional and peripheral areas (e.g., northern Sweden airports) and tourism-dependent developing economies bear disproportionate losses; revenue recycling (Keen et al.) could offset some regressivity only under a tax, not a cap.",8,2,"Climate & Mandates",FALSE,TRUE
60,"Digital ID mandate worldwide","Forces biometric ID for all services to track carbon allowance",-20,-2,1000,"Without, avoid $1T/yr cost + privacy loss; expected global GDP loss $5T","Cato 2025 BCR -2 to -20; Heritage 2024 $5T loss; IMF 2025 multiplier -5×; regression on India Aadhaar BCR; China social credit 2024 $1T/yr cost verified; World Bank 2025 $5T global loss; (-2–-20).",-3,-2,-1,-1,51,,,"partial","C","No published BCR exists for a mandatory worldwide biometric ID used to track carbon allowances, and the author's 'Cato 2025 BCR -2 to -20', 'Heritage 2024 $5T', 'World Bank 2025 $5T global loss' and 'China social credit $1T/yr cost' could not be located. Flag the disagreement: mainstream sources are strongly POSITIVE on voluntary/foundational digital ID (McKinsey 2019: value equal to 3-13% of GDP by 2030; World Bank ID4D; India claims ~Rs 3.48 lakh crore DBT savings), so the author's negative BCR holds only for the specific coercive, carbon-tracking design — supported indirectly by the UK DEFRA 2008 finding that personal carbon allowances would cost £700m-£2bn to set up and £1-2bn/yr to run (~£40/person/yr) and was 'ahead of its time', by Cato/EFF privacy and surveillance critiques (unmonetised costs), and by peer-reviewed evidence that mandatory biometric authentication in India cut some leakage but excluded 1.5-2 million legitimate welfare recipients during the transition.","No source supports $1T/yr. Cost anchors: UK DEFRA (2008) personal carbon trading £0.7-2bn setup + £1-2bn/yr running for the UK alone (~£40 per person per year, excluding time costs); US REAL ID state implementation e.g. California >= $220m initial, Pennsylvania $27m year one then $17-20m/yr (Cato, Harper 2018); Cato estimates a national employment-verification ID ~$20bn initial. Scaling per-capita PCT running costs (~£40/yr) to ~8bn people would imply on the order of $0.4T/yr — an illustrative extrapolation, not a published estimate. Privacy, surveillance and exclusion costs are unmonetised.","Exclusion risk falls on the poor: ID4D reports ~45% of the poorest quintile and 45% of women in low-income countries lack ID (vs 28% richest, 30% men), and Muralidharan et al. document 1.5-2 million Indian welfare beneficiaries losing access during biometric authentication rollout; EFF notes digital-first IDs assume smartphone ownership. Conversely, mainstream sources argue foundational ID mainly benefits the poor (McKinsey: ~65% of value to individuals in emerging economies) — a benefit a voluntary system can deliver without carbon-allowance tracking.",9,2,"Climate & Mandates",FALSE,TRUE
